blocks.prompt: 10. Two cars start together in the same direction from the same place. The first goes with uniform speed of 20km/h. The second goes at a speed of 12km/h in the first hour and increase the speed by 1 km/h each succeeding hour. After how many hours will the second car overtake the first car if both cars go non-stop?
blocks.explanation:
The second car catches the first when both have covered the same total distance.
Car 2 covers 12, 13, 14, ... km in successive hours: an A.P., so its distance is the SUM of an A.P.
Plan: distance of car 1 in \(t\) hours; distance of car 2 as \(S_t\); set them equal; solve.
steps:
Given: Car 1: 20 km each hour. Car 2: 12, 13, 14, ... km in successive hours.
To find: the hours \(t\) after which the distances are equal.
Method: Car 2's distance is \(S_t = \frac{t}{2}[2a_1 + (t - 1)d]\) with \(a_1 = 12\), \(d = 1\).

Distance of the first car
\[\text{Car 1}: 20t \text{ km}\]
Why: Uniform speed 20 km/h for \(t\) hours.

Distance of the second car
\[S_t = \dfrac{t}{2}[2(12) + (t - 1)(1)]\]
\[= \dfrac{t}{2}(t + 23)\]
Why: Hourly distances 12, 13, 14, ... form an A.P. with \(a_1 = 12\), \(d = 1\); \(24 + t - 1 = t + 23\).

Set the distances equal and solve
\[20t = \dfrac{t}{2}(t + 23)\]
\[40 = t + 23\]
\[t = 17\]
Why: Multiply by 2 and divide by \(t\) (allowed since \(t \ne 0\); \(t = 0\) is just the start).

Check
\[\text{Car 1}: 20 \times 17 = 340\]
\[\text{Car 2}: \dfrac{17}{2}(12 + 28) = 340 \;\checkmark\]
Why: In hour 17 car 2 goes \(12 + 16 = 28\) km; both have covered 340 km. After that car 2 is faster, so it moves ahead.
